name: MO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 29 points
Incumbent Wesley Bell running for reelection with a large fundraising advantage
No competitive polling or expert ratings, but prediction markets price Bell near certain to win
Republican challenger Paul Berry has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Bell: a 29-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of more than $3.5 million raised against a challenger with no reported money. Markets price Bell at roughly 98 percent, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or an unexpectedly strong national Republican wave could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Wesley Bell, a first-term Democratic incumbent, seeks reelection in a St. Louis-area district that leans Democratic by roughly 29 points. He faces Republican Paul Berry and Libertarian Tom Schmitz in the general election. Bell has raised about $3.6 million and holds over $1 million on hand, with outside groups spending heavily in his support, while his Republican opponent reports no fundraising activity.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. Prediction markets give Bell about a 98 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong partisan lean, incumbency, and financial dominance makes this seat safely Democratic, with only a remote chance of an upset.
